content: I just can't get over how wronged I feel about being laid off. It's so unjust that my colleague kept their job while I got the boot, even though we were both in similar positions. It feels like they favored him because of some personal connection or bias, and it really hurts to think about all the hard work I put in going down the drain. Everyone keeps telling me to move on, but how can I when it's so clear that this was a decision based on unfairness?

It sounds like you're feeling pretty hurt by the situation. It must be tough seeing your colleague stay while you got laid off, especially with all the effort you put in. Have you had a chance to talk it over with anyone who understands what you're going through?

Yeah, I've talked to a few people, but no one really gets how unfair this feels. They try to offer advice or say things will get better, but they don't understand the depth of my frustration and anger towards those responsible for this decision. It's like they think I should just let it go, but how can I when it was so clearly unjust?

It sounds like you're really holding onto that sense of injustice. It can be tough when others try to offer advice without fully understanding your feelings. Have you thought about maybe writing down all the specifics of what happened or talking to someone who might understand better, like a counselor or another colleague?

I've tried talking to people, but it's hard because they don't see things from my perspective. Writing it down helps sometimes, but it doesn't change how wronged I feel. It's not just about the job; it's about being treated unfairly and seeing someone else benefit while I suffer. How can I move on when this keeps replaying in my head?

It definitely feels tough when you keep replaying what happened. Writing things down can be helpful, as can talking to someone who listens without judgment. Maybe finding a small way to channel your energy into something new could also help shift your focus a bit. What do you think might give you some relief or a sense of accomplishment?

I appreciate that you're trying to help, but it's hard when the core issue is feeling so wronged and seeing no justice for what happened. Starting something new sounds good in theory, but how can I focus on that when all I see is this unfairness staring back at me every day? It feels like everyone around me just wants me to forget about it and move on, but they don't understand the anger and hurt I'm dealing with.

It definitely sounds challenging to keep moving forward when you feel so strongly about what happened. It must be tough having others want you to move on quickly. Have you found any small ways to acknowledge your feelings while still taking steps forward, even if it's just a little bit at a time?

I try to take small steps sometimes, but it’s hard when every step feels like I’m ignoring what happened and how unfair it was. It’s like everyone wants me to sweep my anger under the rug instead of addressing why this made me feel so betrayed. How can I move forward when all I see is injustice? It just doesn’t sit right with me, no matter how much people try to comfort or advise me otherwise.

It sounds really tough to balance moving forward while holding onto those feelings of betrayal and injustice. Maybe finding a way to express your thoughts and emotions regularly could help—whether it's through writing, talking to someone who listens, or another outlet. It might make it easier to take those small steps without feeling like you're ignoring what happened.

Expressing my feelings helps a bit, but it’s not enough when everyone else seems to think I should just move on already. It feels like no one truly understands how unfair this was for me compared to my colleague. How can I find peace with something that feels so fundamentally unjust?
